svg.text: D Standalone sub-mechanisms (2 of 2) — washing, dosing, flipping, portioning
Each panel loops on its own.
source: D-manipulator.md section 7
N7 and the wild ideas N18–N20 are not drawn
N8 Rod car-wash collar
Every retraction washes and wipes the rod. A leak shows as water
at the lantern drain sensor long before it reaches the drive
room.
N11 Spice wand

g.text: spin 1500 rpm: the dose flies off
dip: the wiper strikes it level

svg.text: A pin with a 0.1 mL ring groove is dipped through the lid insert;
the box never travels over the steaming pot, which avoids caking.
N13 Clamshell pan flip

g.text: second pan set upside down on the first
pair turned 180° about the tip bar
top pan lifted off: browned side up

svg.text: Flips pancakes, omelettes, Rösti, fish fillets or a whole pan of
Frikadellen, ≥ 95 % intact, no spatula skill. Costs a second pan
in the wash.
N14 Rinse the board with the recipe water

g.text: measured cooking water as a flume

svg.text: Cut pieces, starch and juice go into the pot with 0 % residue,
and the board arrives at the washer pre-rinsed.
N15 Score before boiling, shrug after

g.text: two silicone cups pull the skin halves off (≈ 5 N)

svg.text: Moves peeling to a state that needs 5 N and no contour following,
and saves 10 % of the potato. Waxy potatoes and tomatoes; not for
raw-potato dishes.
N16 Laser-line portion knife

g.text: feed per cut from the measured cross-section:
thin part → long piece, thick part → short piece

svg.text: As industrial portion cutters do: Frikadellen, goulash cubes,
Schnitzel from a loin, all ±5 % without weighing each piece.
